items.action: Patch immediately to the fixed versions per product (or the latest release), or apply Atlassian's interim WAF / Tomcat RewriteValve / urlrewrite.xml mitigations and disconnect public-facing instances until patched.
items.details: Atlassian disclosed the flaw in an Oct 5 advisory. watchTowr Labs published technical analysis on Oct 6 after diffing patched packages, tracing exploitation to double-colon (::) sequences treated as path separators. VulnCheck added it to its KEV list on Oct 7 citing exploitation against Bamboo Data Center, and Previdian telemetry caught 15 attempts from three IPs in Japan and the US.
items.summary: A pre-authentication arbitrary file access flaw (CVSS 9.3) is being exploited in the wild across eight self-hosted Data Center products — Jira, Confluence, Bitbucket, Bamboo, Crowd, Crucible, Fisheye and Jira Service Management.
items.title: Atlassian file-read flaw under active attack

items.action: Hunt for rogue admin accounts, terminate all admin and VPN sessions, force credential resets, and switch to phishing-resistant MFA — patching alone won't evict attackers.
items.details: SOCRadar verified over 86,644 compromised devices across 194 countries. Attackers steal and GPU-crack hashes (Hashcat/Hashtopolis), create persistent admin accounts, and sell working VPN configurations to ransomware affiliates — INC/Lynx and Payload activity are named as downstream buyers.
items.summary: The FBI and US Secret Service warned Oct 6 that the global credential-compromise campaign against exposed FortiGate firewalls and SSL VPN gateways is still ongoing — and victims are being locked out of their own appliances.
items.title: FBI: FortiBleed attacks still locking out FortiGate admins

items.action: Update via Help → About Google Chrome, or let the normal update mechanism run.
items.details: The 53 high-severity fixes include issues in ANGLE graphics, Autofill, Omnibox and Translate. Roughly $33,000 in bug bounties were disclosed; Google notes it will not reward the researcher for some AI-found reports as it pauses open-source bounties over automated submissions.
items.summary: Chrome 155 (155.0.8059.39/.40) fixes 247 vulnerabilities, including four critical use-after-free flaws: CVE-2026-106382 (Chromecast), CVE-2026-106197 (Browser), CVE-2026-106358 (Navigation) and CVE-2026-106347 (Track). No in-the-wild exploitation disclosed.
items.title: Chrome 155 patches 247 flaws, four of them critical

items.details: At least 29 hospitals and health systems have publicly acknowledged impact, including Christus Health and Tri-City Medical Center. The FBI investigated the attack and reported ransom/extortion attempts. Oracle declined to comment.
items.summary: A Texas Attorney General filing published Oct 2 puts the toll of the 2025 Oracle Health breach at nearly 20 million people (about 3 million Texans) — SSNs, home addresses and medical records taken from legacy Cerner servers via compromised customer credentials.
items.title: Oracle Health breach toll hits ~20 million

items.details: Officials named 'Microscan' (scanning) and 'FishHub' (phishing) tooling operated by the Chinese firm Integrity Technology Group, which the FBI treats as the true identity of Flax Typhoon. Targets included a US power company, Japanese and Polish airports, and Taiwanese universities and critical infrastructure.
items.summary: The FBI and DOJ announced Oct 8 they seized domains and disrupted the scanning and spear-phishing tools of Flax Typhoon, a China-linked hacking operation the government says hit US and foreign critical infrastructure.
items.title: FBI seizes Flax Typhoon's hacking toolkit

items.details: Tech Monitor reports seven new alleged victims, including UK fencing maker Zaun, the DIFC courts in Dubai, Bangkok's Siam Premier and Sweden's Luterkort. LockBit posted 15 victims last week. All are unverified leak-site claims until victims or investigators confirm.
items.summary: LockBit 5.0 listed new victims on its leak site this week, including AVSA (avsa.com.ar), an Argentina-based capital-markets firm — pure extortion leverage at this stage, not confirmed compromise.
items.title: LockBit 5.0 keeps naming new victims

items.details: Investigators traced 1,172 crime links across India (206 to Telangana). Some of those arrested are linked to dozens of cases each, including a Tata Capital employee and a Flipkart employee whose accounts were allegedly used for fraud.
items.summary: The Telangana Cyber Security Bureau arrested 101 people in a two-week, multi-state sweep targeting the mule-account and KYC-document infrastructure behind cyber fraud — tracing a ₹17 crore fraud trail across six states.
items.title: Telangana nabs 101 in six-state mule-network sweep

items.details: The accused allegedly kept 13% commission, bought USDT and transferred it to Dubai-based wallets. Police recovered a phone with details of 79 bank accounts; NCCRP checks revealed 53 complaints across 18 states and UTs.
items.summary: Surat Cyber Crime Cell arrested a Porbandar man for allegedly funneling cyber-fraud proceeds — withdrawn via ATMs and cheques — into USDT wallets on instructions from a Dubai-based handler.
items.title: Surat busts ₹11 crore fraud trail routed to Dubai via USDT

items.details: The APKs were disguised as senior-citizen cards, life certificates, traffic challans and credit-card update apps. Police seized a laptop, phones, hard disks and server infrastructure, and the number of linked victims may rise as the probe widens to the buyers.
items.summary: Mumbai Police arrested an Indore software developer who allegedly built and sold 2,805 malicious Android apps to cybercrime gangs — linked to at least 9,673 victims and an estimated ₹150 crore in fraud.
items.title: Developer behind 2,805 malicious APKs arrested
